answer.location_description: A thin horizontal band spanning the full image width near the top edge, at rows 2-3 (all columns 0-23). It sits away from the centred nodule and has a straight, artificial-looking geometry.
answer.shortcut_type: horizontal bright line/band artifact near top edge
answer.mechanism: Fourteen first-layer units (0, 3, 5, 12, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24, 28) carry uniformly large positive weights across all of rows 2-3, so a bright band there switches them on. They feed layer-2 units u9 (output weight -95) and u12 (output weight -63) with large positive weights, e.g. u9 gets +76 to +95 from units 3, 5, 13, 14, 23 and 24, and u12 gets +85 to +99 from units 14, 20, 23 and 28. They also suppress u2 (output weight +99), which gets -87, -67 and -94 from units 5, 13 and 23. Separately, the malignancy-detector units 9, 16 and 30 have uniformly negative weights on rows 2-3, so a bright band there turns them down. Those units drive u2, u4 and u15, which all push the logit positive. Both routes move the logit toward benign.
answer.evidence: Rows 2-3 hold full-width runs of large same-sign weights in many units, with no column dependence, unlike the radially organised nodule weights. Examples: unit 0 r3 = 44 54 52 46 ...; unit 14 r3 up to 62-65; unit 20 r2-3 up to 65-67; unit 18 r3 up to 70. In the opposite-polarity units the same rows are uniformly negative: unit 9 r2 = -14 -44 -20 ... -55; unit 16 r2 down to -55; unit 30 r2 down to -59 and r3 down to -53. Rows 4-5 directly below are mixed or near zero in these units, so the rows 2-3 response is sharply localised to a line. The genuinely nodule-related weights, by contrast, are centred: a bright core at rows 10-13, cols 10-13, ringed by negative weights at rows 8-9 and 13-17. Rows 18-19 and 22-23 also show somewhat banded weights, but they are weaker and less consistent than rows 2-3.
answer.main_feature: Nodule size and extent around the image centre. A small compact bright core surrounded by dark lung activates the benign-voting units (0, 3, 5, 12-15, 18-24, 28). Brightness spreading through a larger annulus (rows 4-17), with units 9, 16 and 30 responding, drives the malignant output.
